beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy you're here.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, you solved logic puzzles, one clue at a time. And with that, you finished all of Unit two. Give yourself a big pat on the back!
beats.caption: Unit 2 · Logic & Reasoning · done!

beats.vo: Today, we're starting Unit three. It's called, Shapes, Grids, and Coordinates.
beats.caption: Unit 3 · Shapes, Grids & Coordinates

beats.vo: And chapter one is called, Shapes All Around!
beats.caption: Chapter 1 · Shapes All Around

beats.vo: By the end, you'll be able to name a shape, just by counting. Ready? Let's go!
beats.caption: Name a shape, just by counting!

beats.vo: Meet Aarav. He's in class four, and he loves a good challenge.
beats.caption: Meet Aarav!

beats.vo: One morning, his teacher says, find as many shapes in our classroom as you can, in one minute! Ready, steady, go!
beats.caption: "Find shapes in the classroom, in 1 minute!"

beats.vo: Aarav looks around. The blackboard. The clock on the wall. The carrom board in the corner. Shapes everywhere!
beats.caption: Blackboard, clock, carrom board…

beats.vo: But wait. How do you know what a shape is called? What's the secret? Think about it.
beats.caption: How do you know a shape's name? Think!

beats.vo: The secret is counting! Count the straight sides, and count the corners. Those numbers tell you the name.
beats.caption: Count the sides and the corners!

beats.vo: First, a few shape words. A two D shape is a flat shape, one you can draw on paper. Like a square, or a circle.
beats.caption: 2D shape = a flat shape you can draw

beats.vo: A side is a straight edge of a shape. Let's count this triangle's sides. One, two, three.
beats.caption: Side = a straight edge

beats.vo: A corner is the point where two sides meet. One, two, three corners! A corner has another name too, vertex. And when there's more than one, we say, vertices.
beats.caption: Corner = where 2 sides meet (a vertex)

beats.vo: So a triangle has three sides, and three corners. Tri means three, just like a tricycle has three wheels!
beats.caption: Triangle: 3 sides, 3 corners

beats.vo: Now, a square. Count its sides with me. One, two, three, four. And look, all four sides are exactly the same length. That's what makes it a square.
beats.caption: Square: 4 sides, all equal

beats.vo: A rectangle has four sides too. But they're not all the same. The two long sides match each other. And the two short sides match each other. Just like a door!
beats.caption: Rectangle: 4 sides, opposite sides equal

beats.vo: That's the big difference. A square has all four sides equal. A rectangle only has its opposite sides equal.
beats.caption: Square: all 4 equal · Rectangle: opposite

beats.vo: And a circle? It's just one smooth, curvy line. No straight sides, and no corners. Nothing to count! Just like a roti, or a bangle.
beats.caption: Circle: no sides, no corners

beats.vo: Here's where it gets fun. More sides means a new name!
beats.caption: More sides → a new name!

beats.vo: Five sides? That's a pentagon. Count with me. One, two, three, four, five.
beats.caption: Pentagon: 5 sides

beats.vo: Six sides is a hexagon. Bees build their honeycomb out of hexagons! Every little cell has six sides, and six corners.
beats.caption: Hexagon: 6 sides, like a honeycomb cell

beats.vo: And eight sides? That's an octagon. Octo means eight, just like an octopus has eight arms!
beats.caption: Octagon: 8 sides. Octopus: 8 arms!

beats.vo: Here's a handy tip. In these shapes, the sides and corners are always the same number. Five sides, five corners. Six sides, six corners. Eight sides, eight corners.
beats.caption: Tip: same number of sides and corners

beats.vo: Game time! Let's name that shape.
beats.caption: Game: name that shape!

beats.vo: Near Aarav's school, there's a red sign that says, stop. Count its sides. What shape is it? Pause, and count.
beats.caption: Count the STOP sign's sides. What shape?

beats.vo: Eight sides! So a stop sign is an octagon. Eight sides, and eight corners. Did you count them all?
beats.caption: 8 sides → an octagon!

beats.vo: Now, true or false? A triangle has four corners. Hmm. Think carefully.
beats.caption: True or false: a triangle has 4 corners?

beats.vo: False! A triangle has three sides, so it has three corners. Not four.
beats.caption: False! 3 sides → 3 corners

beats.vo: Now, remember Aarav's challenge? Let's help him name each shape, by counting.
beats.caption: Back to Aarav's shape hunt!

beats.vo: The blackboard. Four sides, two long and two short. It's a rectangle!
beats.caption: Blackboard → rectangle

beats.vo: The wall clock. One curvy line, and no corners. A circle!
beats.caption: Wall clock → circle

beats.vo: The samosa in his tiffin. Three sides, three corners. A triangle! Yum.
beats.caption: Samosa → triangle. Yum!

beats.vo: And the carrom board. Four equal sides. A square!
beats.caption: Carrom board → square

beats.vo: Now you try. Look around your room. How many rectangles can you spot in one minute? Doors, windows, books!
beats.caption: Your turn: how many rectangles around you?

beats.vo: Shapes are on every screen too! Zoom in really close, and a screen picture is made of tiny squares of light, called pixels.
beats.caption: Screens are made of tiny squares: pixels

beats.vo: In a video game, a house can be built from just two shapes. A square for the walls, and a triangle for the roof.
beats.caption: Game house = square + triangle roof

beats.vo: So how many sides altogether? The square has four. The triangle has three. Four plus three, equals seven sides!
beats.caption: 4 + 3 = 7 sides altogether

beats.vo: Ready for a harder one? Aarav's classroom wall has two square windows, and one triangle flag. How many sides altogether? Take your time.
beats.caption: 2 square windows + 1 triangle flag = ? sides

beats.vo: Each square has four sides. Four plus four is eight. Add the triangle's three, and that makes eleven sides!
beats.caption: 4 + 4 + 3 = 11 sides

beats.vo: One more. How many corners do one hexagon and one triangle have, together?
beats.caption: Hexagon + triangle: how many corners?

beats.vo: The hexagon has six corners. The triangle has three. Six plus three, equals nine corners!
beats.caption: 6 + 3 = 9 corners

beats.vo: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: How many sides does a hexagon have? Pause the video, and draw one on paper if you like.
beats.caption: How many sides does a hexagon have?

beats.vo: Six sides! And six corners too, just like one cell of a honeycomb. Did you get it? Brilliant!
beats.caption: 6 sides and 6 corners, like a honeycomb cell

beats.vo: Let's remember. Count the sides, to name the shape.
beats.caption: Count the sides to name the shape

beats.vo: A square has four equal sides. A rectangle has opposite sides equal.
beats.caption: Square: 4 equal · Rectangle: opposite equal

beats.vo: Triangle three. Pentagon five. Hexagon six. Octagon eight.
beats.caption: Triangle 3 · Pentagon 5 · Hexagon 6 · Octagon 8

beats.vo: And a circle has no sides, and no corners.
beats.caption: Circle: no sides, no corners

beats.vo: Chapter one of Unit three, done! You're a real shape detective now, champ.
beats.caption: Chapter 1 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
